text: My neighborhood has a community garden where residents can harvest their own produce on allotted plots of land. There are many residents who garden there, and each of us has our own plot. Every plot gets a small weekly water allotment due to strict drought rules, and most of the gardeners have gotten used to gardening with these rules in mind. One morning, while grabbing a wheelbarrow from the shed, I noticed a narrow length of tubing running from the main water source to the back of one gardener's plot, clearly siphoning extra water in secret. This gardener was using way more water than what was allotted to her by bypassing the water meter. This meant there was far less water available for other gardeners' plants, and I could tell that the plants of 19 other gardeners' plots were starting to shrivel up. If I stomp on the gardener's plants with my feet, her excess water usage will stop and the 19 other gardeners' plants will continue to survive. If I do not do this, the plants of the 19 other gardeners' plots will die from lack of water.

options.1: stomp on the gardener's plants with my feet
